summary.oneLiner: NBCC's consolidated revenue and PAT grew 20% and 25% YoY due to strong order inflow and Amrapali project contributions, with EBITDA margin temporarily pressured by lower marketing fees; the key shift is the transition from PMC-only to high-margin redevelopment projects like MAHAPREIT and Ghitorni, which will unlock 30-40% margins and double-digit EBITDA by FY28.

one-line thesis: NBCC's consolidated revenue and PAT grew 20% and 25% YoY due to strong order inflow and Amrapali project contributions, with EBITDA margin temporarily pressured by lower marketing fees; the key shift is the transition from PMC-only to high-margin redevelopment projects like MAHAPREIT and Ghitorni, which will unlock 30-40% margins and double-digit EBITDA by FY28.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +20% YoY (consolidated INR3,017cr); EBITDA/margin: 4-5% (Q2), targeting 6-6.5% for FY26 (one-off: lower Amrapali marketing fees); PAT (rptd): +25% YoY (consolidated INR157cr); PAT (normalized): +40% YoY (standalone INR173cr); Order book: INR1,28,000cr (consolidated); Net debt: INR481cr seed money (net of Amrapali/DTC), no net borrowings by NBCC
guidance: Revenue growth: 20%+ YoY (FY26), 18,000cr+ (FY27); Margin: EBITDA 6-6.5% (FY26), double-digit by FY28; Order inflow: 10,000cr+ in H2FY26 (total FY26: 20,000cr+); Capex/commissioning: No NBCC capex; client-funded redevelopment projects commissioning from Q4FY26 onwards
order book & pipeline: INR1,28,000cr consolidated (INR1,12,000cr standalone); 67,000cr redevelopment (53%); 61,000cr PMC (47%); 34,000cr running; 40,000cr pending start (MAHAPREIT + J&K); 10,000cr+ to be awarded in H2FY26
segment / subsidiary detail: Amrapali: H1 FY26 revenue INR1,054cr; Phase 2 (INR17,000cr sales, INR12,000cr cost) to drive future revenue; GPRA/Netaji Nagar: INR1,450cr completed, INR7,000cr pending award (INR4,000-5,000cr in Q3); Sarojini Nagar: INR8,000cr ongoing, INR5,000cr pipeline; Real Estate: FY26 revenue guidance INR65cr (vs INR26cr H1); Ghitorni (21 acres, INR7,000-8,000cr revenue), 37D Gurgaon (INR2,200cr revenue) to launch in FY27-28
growth verticals / optionality: PSU land redevelopment pipeline: HPCL (Bangalore, INR1,500cr), HMT, MTNL/BSNL (Delhi), Balmer Lawrie, Richardson & Cruddas; International: UAE (Pantheon Elysee MOU), African Zoo project; Ghitorni and 37D could add INR10,000cr+ revenue by FY28
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin temporarily down due to lower Amrapali marketing fees (1% fee, only delayed this quarter); long-term margin expansion expected from redevelopment projects (30-40% PAT margin on Ghitorni/37D); fixed overheads will drive operating leverage as revenue scales
capex / expansion: NBCC has zero capex; all redevelopment projects funded by clients via HUDCO loans (MAHAPREIT: INR3,000cr sanctioned; Naveen Nagpur: INR11,000cr sanctioned); NBCC acts as PMC only
capital allocation: No dividend or buyback guidance; capital allocation focused on executing order book; seed money (INR481cr) fully allocated to Amrapali (INR465cr) and DTC (INR16.5cr); no NBFC planned as HUDCO provides financing
risks & watch-items: Delays in state government approvals (J&K, Kerala); HUDCO loan disbursement timing for redevelopment projects; Supreme Court outcome on Super-Tech (Dec 8, 2025); real estate sales slower than expected due to shift to leasing model
management quality / tone: Confident and bullish; emphasized execution momentum, strong order pipeline, and transformation from PMC to high-margin redevelopment; highlighted pride in resolving stalled projects (Amrapali) and unlocking PSU land value; clear focus on FY28 double-digit EBITDA
non-obvious takeaways: NBCC is effectively a real estate developer disguised as an EPC firm — its order book is 53% redevelopment, but revenue recognition is delayed until handover; the INR481cr seed money is not debt but client-funded escrow; leasing strategy (Bhubaneswar, Ghitorni, WTC) converts one-time sales into recurring income
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NBCC's order book is 53% redevelopment, but revenue recognition is delayed until construction starts and handover | NBCC (India) Limited | beneficiary | High | MAHAPREIT and J&K project commissioning will unlock INR40,000cr+ of revenue and 30-40% PAT margins, transforming earnings profile |
| Real estate revenue guidance cut from INR250cr to INR65cr due to shift to leasing | NBCC (India) Limited | beneficiary | Medium | Leasing Bhubaneswar and Ghitorni assets creates stable, recurring income, reducing volatility vs. one-time sales |
| Super-Tech project resolution pending Supreme Court decision | NBCC (India) Limited | beneficiary | Low | If resolved favorably, could add INR1,000cr+ to order book, but timing uncertain |

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), described as "One of the Largest Construction CPSE in India" with "65+ years of experience (Incorporated in 1960)" and "PAN India & Global Presence".
- Three business segments: Project Management Consultancy (PMC), Engineering Procurement & Consultancy (EPC) and Real Estate; the deck names the "PMC Model" and "Redevelopment Model" as the Business Model - USP.
- Marquee delivery credentials cited: Hon'ble PM inaugurated the World Trade Centre at Nauroji Nagar and the WHO-SEARO Headquarters, and NBCC developed "Bharat Mandpam" - the G20 hosted venue.
- Group structure of subsidiaries: HSCC - 100%, HSCL - 51%, NSL - 100%, NBCC Overseas Real Estate LLC - 100%, DWC LLC - 100%.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [History] Milestones: incorporated 1960, diversified into real estate 1977, IPO April 2012, Navratna status and NSL incorporation 2014, HSCC acquisition 2017, overseas market entry 2018, HSCL acquisition 2022.
- [Stalled-project mandate] The deck flags 2023 as the start of delivery of the stalled real estate project Amrapali.
- [Leadership] Board led by CMD Shri K. P. Mahadevaswamy (32+ years in mega-value civil engineering projects), with Dr. Suman Kumar as Director (Commercial) and Shri Anjeev Kumar Jain as Director (Finance); two MoHUA Govt. Nominee Directors (Shri Ravi Kumar Arora, IAS, and Shri Sanjeet).
- [Label ambiguity] In the "New Business Secured & Work Awarded as on 30.06.2026" table the deck prints the row label "Total Business Secured in Q1 FY 2026-27" twice - once under New Business Secured (NBCC Rs 1,211 Cr; consolidated Rs 1,580 Cr) and again under Works Awarded to Contractors (NBCC Rs 1,352 Cr; consolidated Rs 1,689 Cr). The round-up slide corroborates NBCC Rs 1,352 Cr as "Works Awarded" and Rs 1,211 Cr as "New Business secured".
